title: Parts of a Table (Print Only)

illustrates.quote: Parts of a Table. For our purposes, the parts of a table are: Column Headings: Headings across the top of the table Separation Line: Line between a column heading and column entry Row Headings: Headings listed vertically on the left and/or right side of the table Column Entries: Intersections of a row and a column Guide Dots: A series of dot 5s leading the reader from one column to the next or indicating an empty column entry.

print.notes: This is a schematic/generic diagram, not a table of real data: every cell literally contains the placeholder label naming the part it illustrates ("Column Heading", "Column Subheading", "Row Heading", "Row Subheading", "Column Entry"), boxed with ruled lines.
print.surroundingText: 11.2.2 Parts of a Table (defines the five terms) precedes the example; 11.2.3 ("Tables have a relationship between columns and rows...") follows it.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box (outer border plus internal rules separating the column-heading row from the sub-heading row, and the row-heading column from the entries). "Column Heading", "Column Subheading" and "Row Heading" text is bold; "Row Subheading" is bold and indented under the row-heading column; "Column Entry" text is plain (not bold).

braille.notes: No braille is given for this example; the heading is explicitly labelled '(Print Only)' and the .txt extraction contains no dot-pattern block between this heading and the start of 11.2.3.
